name: S&P 500 trailing P/E ratio
why: Index price divided by trailing 12-month as-reported earnings. Automatically loads up to 20 years of monthly history and the latest estimate from Multpl. Revised history, not first-release data. Do not mix forward P/E or CAPE. High ratios indicate valuation sensitivity, not a stand-alone downturn timing signal; earnings near zero can distort P/E.

rights: Use permitted source data; preserve methodology and observation dates
name: S&P 500 price-to-cash-flow ratio
source: State Street S&P 500 index characteristics / licensed history
why: Automatically reads Price/Cash Flow and its observation date from State Street S&P 500 Index Characteristics. Each refresh retains previous snapshots to build history from the first connection; no 20-year backfill is available. Uses the provider cash-flow and aggregation methodology, not free cash flow or SPY fund statistics. Revised snapshots are not first-release data. Elevated multiples alone do not time a downturn.
